verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the December crash and the matching Q4 crash. For valid inputs they produce the same results, keep existing behavior, and add the same regression tests. A uses a small, explicit helper that only handles month 13. B uses the common year/month modulo idiom and builds quarter_range on top of month_range, which reuses existing code but reads a little less directly. Both reports are accurate, so I would be equally happy to merge either.
a_issues: _first_of_month only special-cases month 13, so its name suggests a more general helper than it is.
b_issues: The `year + month // 12, month % 12 + 1` arithmetic is correct but takes a moment to check.
Getting quarter_range's end via `month_range(year, 3 * quarter)` is indirect and builds a start date that is thrown away.

verdict.rationale: Both fixes are correct for every valid month and quarter, both also fix the Q4 bug, and both add the same regression tests. A changes less: it fixes the month arithmetic in one place and has `quarter_range` reuse `month_range`, so it adds no new helper. B's `_first_of_month` helper is readable but special-cases only month 13, which makes it a narrow helper that adds code. A's report also openly says it did not confirm the new tests fail on the old code.
a_issues: The `month // 12` and `month % 12 + 1` arithmetic is a little less obvious at a glance than an explicit December check, and it has no comment.
The regression tests were not confirmed to fail against the old code (the report says so).
b_issues: Adds a new helper that handles only `month == 13`, which is narrow and less general than plain rollover arithmetic.
`quarter_range` duplicates the rollover logic through the helper instead of reusing `month_range`.
